title: NEET 2020 Biology Official Examination
subtitle: National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET-UG 2020) • Biology Section

questions.question: If the distance between two consecutive base pairs is 0.34 nm and the total number of base pairs of a DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell is 6.6 × 10⁹ bp, then the length of the DNA is approximately:
questions.explanation: Each base pair contributes 0.34 nm. Thus, total length = 6.6 × 10⁹ × 0.34 nm = 2.244 × 10⁹ nm = approximately 2.2 m.

questions.unit: Unit I: Diversity in the Living World
questions.question: Bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate animals are exemplified by:
questions.explanation: Members of Platyhelminthes are bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate animals. Their body does not possess a true coelom.

questions.unit: Unit I: Diversity in the Living World
questions.question: Match the following columns and select the correct option.
table: (b) Adult with radial symmetry and larva with bilateral symmetry
questions.explanation: Locusta is a gregarious, polyphagous pest; Asterias has radial adult symmetry and bilateral larvae; scorpions possess book lungs; Ctenoplana exhibits bioluminescence.

questions.unit: Unit III: Cell – Structure and Functions
questions.question: Which is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, packages and helps form glycoproteins and glycolipids.

questions.question: The QRS complex in a standard ECG represents:
questions.explanation: The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarisation, which initiates ventricular contraction.

questions.question: Match the following columns and select the correct option.
table: (i) Located between second and seventh ribs
(iv) Do not connect with the sternum
questions.explanation: Floating ribs do not attach to the sternum. The acromion articulates with the clavicle, the scapula lies opposite the second to seventh ribs, and the glenoid cavity articulates with the head of the humerus.

questions.question: Experimental verification of the chromosomal theory of inheritance was done by:
questions.explanation: Sutton and Boveri proposed the chromosomal theory, while Thomas Hunt Morgan experimentally verified it using Drosophila.

questions.unit: Unit II: Structural Organisation in Plants and Animals
questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement.
choices: Sapwood is involved in conduction of water and minerals from root to leaf.
Sapwood is the innermost secondary xylem and is lighter in colour.
Due to deposition of tannins, resins, oils, etc., heart wood is dark in colour.
Heart wood does not conduct water but gives mechanical support.
questions.answerText: Sapwood is the innermost secondary xylem and is lighter in colour.
questions.explanation: Sapwood is the outer secondary xylem, not the innermost. It conducts water and minerals. Heartwood is the inner, darker, non-conducting region that provides mechanical support.

questions.question: Match the following columns and select the correct option.
questions.explanation: Pituitary-related ADH deficiency causes diabetes insipidus; hyperthyroidism can cause Graves' disease; adrenal insufficiency causes Addison's disease; insufficient insulin causes diabetes mellitus.

questions.question: Match the organism with its use in biotechnology.
questions.topic: Tools and organisms used in biotechnology
questions.explanation: B. thuringiensis produces Cry proteins; T. aquaticus provides Taq DNA polymerase; A. tumefaciens is used as a cloning vector; S. typhimurium was involved in the construction of the first recombinant DNA molecule.

questions.unit: Unit III: Cell – Structure and Functions
questions.question: Identify the substances having glycosidic bond and peptide bond, respectively in their structure:
questions.explanation: Inulin is a polysaccharide containing glycosidic linkages, whereas insulin is a protein whose amino acids are connected by peptide bonds.

questions.question: Name the enzyme that facilitates opening of DNA helix during transcription.
questions.explanation: During transcription, RNA polymerase binds to the promoter and facilitates local unwinding of DNA so that the template strand can be transcribed.

questions.question: If the head of cockroach is removed, it may live for few days because:
choices: the cockroach does not have nervous system.
the head holds a small proportion of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral part of its body.
the head holds a 1/3rd of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the dorsal part of its body.
the supra-oesophageal ganglia of the cockroach are situated in ventral part of abdomen.
questions.answerText: the head holds a small proportion of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral part of its body.
questions.explanation: Most of the cockroach's nervous system consists of a ventral nerve cord and segmental ganglia, so removal of the head does not immediately stop all nervous activity.

questions.question:
Select the correct events that occur during inspiration.
(a) Contraction of diaphragm
(b) Contraction of external inter-costal muscles
(c) Pulmonary volume decreases
(d) Intra pulmonary pressure increases
questions.explanation: During inspiration, the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles contract. Thoracic volume increases, pulmonary pressure decreases and air enters the lungs.

questions.unit: Unit VIII: Biology in Human Welfare
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.question: By which method was a new breed ‘Hisardale’ of sheep formed by using Bikaneri ewes and Marino rams?
questions.explanation: Hisardale was developed by crossing Bikaneri ewes with Marino rams, making it an example of cross breeding.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the most abundant protein in the animals?
questions.explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in animals and forms an important component of connective tissues.

questions.question: How many true breeding pea plant varieties did Mendel select as pairs, which were similar except in one character with contrasting traits?
questions.explanation: Mendel selected 14 true-breeding pea varieties, arranged as seven pairs showing contrasting traits.

questions.question: The body of the ovule is fused within the funicle at:
questions.explanation: The hilum is the point where the body of the ovule is attached to the funicle.

questions.unit: Unit VIII: Biology in Human Welfare
questions.question: Which of the following is correct about viroids?
choices: They have free RNA without protein coat.
They have DNA with protein coat.
They have free DNA without protein coat.
They have RNA with protein coat.
questions.answerText: They have free RNA without protein coat.
questions.explanation: Viroids are small infectious RNA molecules without a protein coat.

questions.question: The number of substrate level phosphorylations in one turn of citric acid cycle is:
questions.explanation: One molecule of GTP is produced by substrate-level phosphorylation during conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate.

questions.question: The product(s) of reaction catalyzed by nitrogenase in root nodules of leguminous plants is/are:
questions.explanation: Nitrogenase catalyses the reduction of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia (NH₃) during biological nitrogen fixation.

questions.unit: Unit VIII: Biology in Human Welfare
questions.question: Match the following diseases with the causative organism and select the correct option.
questions.explanation: Typhoid is caused by Salmonella typhi, pneumonia by Haemophilus, filariasis by Wuchereria, and malaria by Plasmodium.

questions.question: From his experiments, S.L. Miller produced amino acids by mixing the following in a closed flask:
choices: CH₃, H₂, NH₄ and water vapor at 800°C
CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapor at 600°C
CH₃, H₂, NH₃ and water vapor at 600°C
CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapor at 800°C
questions.answerText: CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapor at 800°C
questions.explanation: Miller's experiment used a reducing atmosphere containing methane, hydrogen, ammonia and water vapour, with electrical sparks simulating lightning.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: Adenine pairs with thymine through one H-bond.
Adenine pairs with thymine through three H-bonds.
Adenine does not pair with thymine.
Adenine pairs with thymine through two H-bonds.
questions.answerText: Adenine pairs with thymine through two H-bonds.
questions.explanation: In DNA, adenine and thymine form two hydrogen bonds, while guanine and cytosine form three.

questions.question: Match the following with respect to meiosis:
questions.explanation: Synapsis occurs in zygotene, crossing over in pachytene, chiasmata become visible in diplotene, and terminalization occurs during diakinesis.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair from the following:
choices: Polymerases – Break the DNA into fragments
Nucleases – Separate the two strands of DNA
Exonucleases – Make cuts at specific positions within DNA
Ligases – Join the two DNA molecules
questions.answerText: Ligases – Join the two DNA molecules
questions.topic: Enzymes used in recombinant DNA technology
questions.explanation: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds, allowing DNA molecules/fragments to be joined.

questions.unit: Unit VIII: Biology in Human Welfare
questions.question: Select the option including all sexually transmitted diseases.
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea, syphilis and genital herpes are all sexually transmitted infections/diseases. Malaria and filariasis are not STDs.

questions.question: Embryological support for evolution was disapproved by:
questions.explanation: Karl Ernst von Baer criticised the idea that embryonic development directly recapitulates evolutionary history, which challenged the use of embryology as originally proposed in support of evolution.

questions.unit: Unit II: Structural Organisation in Plants and Animals
questions.question: The roots that originate from the base of the stem are:
questions.explanation: Prop roots arise from the branches/stem and grow downward into the soil, providing additional mechanical support. The banyan tree is a common example.

questions.question: In gel electrophoresis, separated DNA fragments can be visualized with the help of:
questions.explanation: DNA fragments separated by gel electrophoresis are stained with ethidium bromide and visualized under UV radiation, where the DNA bands fluoresce.

questions.question: Which of the following hormone levels will cause release of ovum (ovulation) from the Graafian follicle?
questions.explanation: A high level of estrogen produced by the mature Graafian follicle causes a positive feedback effect on the pituitary, resulting in the LH surge, which triggers ovulation.

questions.unit: Unit II: Structural Organisation in Plants and Animals
questions.question: Goblet cells of alimentary canal are modified from:
questions.explanation: Goblet cells are specialized columnar epithelial cells that secrete mucus, which protects and lubricates the lining of the alimentary canal.

questions.question: Snow-blindness in Antarctic region is due to:
choices: Inflammation of cornea due to high dose of UV-B radiation
High reflection of light from snow
Damage to retina caused by infra-red rays
Freezing of fluids in the eye by low temperature
questions.answerText: Inflammation of cornea due to high dose of UV-B radiation
questions.explanation: Excessive exposure to UV-B radiation can cause inflammation and damage to the cornea, producing snow blindness.

questions.question: Match the following concerning essential elements and their functions in plants:
questions.topic: Essential mineral elements and their functions
questions.explanation: Iron is involved in chlorophyll biosynthesis; zinc is required for IAA synthesis; boron is important for pollen germination; manganese participates in photolysis of water during photosynthesis.

questions.question: Bt cotton variety that was developed by the introduction of toxin gene of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is resistant to:
questions.explanation: Bt cotton contains genes from Bacillus thuringiensis that produce Cry proteins, which are toxic to certain insect pests.

questions.unit: Unit II: Structural Organisation in Plants and Animals
questions.question: Ray florets have:
questions.explanation: Ray florets of members of Asteraceae possess an inferior ovary.

questions.question: Montreal protocol was signed in 1987 for control of:
choices: Transport of Genetically modified organisms from one country to another
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol (1987) was an international agreement designed to control and phase out substances responsible for depletion of the ozone layer, particularly CFCs.

questions.question: Identify the wrong statement with regard to Restriction Enzymes.
choices: They cut the strand of DNA at palindromic sites.
They are useful in genetic engineering.
Sticky ends can be joined by using DNA ligases.
Each restriction enzyme functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence.
questions.answerText: Each restriction enzyme functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence.
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes recognize specific nucleotide sequences, often palindromic sequences, and cut DNA at or near those sites. They do not function by simply inspecting the length of DNA.

questions.unit: Unit VIII: Biology in Human Welfare
questions.question: The infectious stage of Plasmodium that enters the human body is:
questions.explanation: When an infected female Anopheles mosquito bites a human, it injects sporozoites into the bloodstream. These initiate the infection in humans.

questions.question: Meiotic division of the secondary oocyte is completed:
choices: At the time of fusion of a sperm with an ovum
questions.answerText: At the time of fusion of a sperm with an ovum
questions.explanation: The secondary oocyte is arrested at metaphase II. It completes meiosis II only after sperm entry, during fertilisation.

questions.question: The oxygenation activity of RuBisCO enzyme in C₃ photosynthetic leaf leads to the formation of:
choices: 1 molecule of 4-C compound and 1 molecule of 2-C compound
questions.answerText: 1 molecule of 4-C compound and 1 molecule of 2-C compound
questions.explanation: During oxygenation, RuBisCO adds O₂ to RuBP, producing one molecule of 3-phosphoglycerate (3-C) and one molecule of 2-phosphoglycolate (2-C).Note: The wording/options in the paper appear inconsistent with the standard biochemical products; the option structure does not exactly represent the usual 3-C + 2-C products.

questions.unit: Unit I: Diversity in the Living World
questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true for the phylum-Chordata?
Question statements:
(a) In Urochordata notochord extends from head to tail and it is present throughout their life.
(b) In Vertebrata notochord is present during the embryonic period only.
(c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow.
(d) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla: Hemichordata, Tunicata and Cephalochordata.
questions.explanation: In vertebrates, the notochord is present during embryonic development and is replaced by the vertebral column in adults. Chordates have a dorsal, hollow nerve cord. Statement (a) is incorrect for Urochordata because the notochord occurs only in the larval tail.

questions.unit: Unit VIII: Biology in Human Welfare
questions.question: Match the following columns and select the correct option.
questions.explanation: Clostridium butyricum produces butyric acid; Trichoderma polysporum produces cyclosporin-A; Monascus purpureus produces statins that lower blood cholesterol; Aspergillus niger produces citric acid.

questions.unit: Unit I: Diversity in the Living World
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is of unicellular algae?
questions.explanation: Chlorella and Spirulina are commonly included among unicellular/single-celled algal or cyanobacterial forms used as single-cell protein sources. Gelidium, Gracilaria, Laminaria and Sargassum are multicellular forms.

questions.question: In light reaction, plastoquinone facilitates the transfer of electrons from:
questions.explanation: Plastoquinone acts as an electron carrier between Photosystem II and the cytochrome b₆f complex in the thylakoid electron transport chain.

questions.question: Presence of which of the following conditions in urine are indicative of Diabetes Mellitus?
questions.explanation: Diabetes mellitus can result in glucose in urine (glycosuria). Increased fat breakdown can also produce ketone bodies, resulting in ketonuria.

questions.question: Secondary metabolites such as nicotine, strychnine and caffeine are produced by plants for their:
questions.explanation: Many secondary metabolites such as nicotine, strychnine and caffeine have protective roles and help plants defend themselves against herbivores and other threats.

questions.question: Which of the following would help in prevention of diuresis?
choices: Reabsorption of Na⁺ and water from renal tubules due to aldosterone
Decrease in secretion of renin by JG cells
More water reabsorption due to undersecretion of ADH
questions.answerText: Reabsorption of Na⁺ and water from renal tubules due to aldosterone
questions.explanation: Aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption in the renal tubules. Water follows sodium osmotically, thereby helping reduce water loss and diuresis.

questions.question: Select the correct match.
choices: Sickle cell anaemia — Autosomal recessive trait, chromosome-11
questions.answerText: Sickle cell anaemia — Autosomal recessive trait, chromosome-11
questions.explanation: Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by a mutation in the β-globin gene located on chromosome 11.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an attribute of a population?
questions.explanation: Natality, mortality and sex ratio are population attributes. Species interactions such as competition, predation and mutualism describe relationships between populations rather than being direct population attributes.

questions.unit: Unit III: Cell – Structure and Functions
questions.question: Which of the following statements about inclusion bodies is incorrect?
choices: These are involved in ingestion of food particles.
They lie free in the cytoplasm.
These represent reserve material in cytoplasm.
They are not bound by any membrane.
questions.answerText: These are involved in ingestion of food particles.
questions.explanation: Inclusion bodies are non-living structures present freely in the cytoplasm and may store reserve materials. They are not involved in ingestion of food particles.

questions.unit: Unit II: Structural Organisation in Plants and Animals
questions.question:
The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features:
(a) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath.
(b) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue.
(c) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed.
(d) Phloem parenchyma absent.
Identify the category of plant and its part:
questions.explanation: A monocot stem has scattered, conjoint and closed vascular bundles, a large parenchymatous ground tissue and generally lacks phloem parenchyma.

questions.question: In relation to Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity of an ecosystem, which one of the following statements is correct?
choices: Gross primary productivity is always more than net primary productivity.
Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity are one and same.
There is no relationship between Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity.
Gross primary productivity is always less than net primary productivity.
questions.answerText: Gross primary productivity is always more than net primary productivity.
questions.explanation: NPP = GPP − Respiration losses. Therefore, net primary productivity is lower than gross primary productivity.

questions.question: In water hyacinth and water lily, pollination takes place by:
questions.explanation: Water-associated plants such as water hyacinth and water lily are not necessarily hydrophilous; their pollination can involve insects and water-associated mechanisms.

questions.unit: Unit VIII: Biology in Human Welfare
questions.question: Which of the following is put into Anaerobic sludge digester for further sewage treatment?
questions.explanation: During secondary sewage treatment, activated sludge is generated. A portion is returned to the aeration tank and the remaining sludge is sent to anaerobic sludge digesters.

questions.question: The process responsible for facilitating loss of water in liquid form from the tip of grass blades at night and in early morning is:
questions.explanation: Loss of water in liquid form from leaf tips is called guttation. It is caused by positive root pressure, particularly at night or early morning when transpiration is low.

questions.unit: Unit II: Structural Organisation in Plants and Animals
questions.question: Cuboidal epithelium with brush border of microvilli is found in:
questions.explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) is lined by cuboidal epithelium with a brush border of microvilli, increasing the surface area for reabsorption.

questions.question: Select the correct statement.
choices: Insulin acts on pancreatic cells and adipocytes.
questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids promote gluconeogenesis, increasing blood glucose availability. Insulin generally lowers blood glucose, while glucagon acts primarily to raise blood glucose.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an inhibitory substance governing seed dormancy?
questions.topic: Seed dormancy and plant growth regulators
questions.explanation: Abscisic acid (ABA) promotes seed dormancy. Gibberellins generally promote germination and overcome dormancy, so gibberellic acid is not an inhibitory substance governing seed dormancy.

questions.question: According to Robert May, the global species diversity is about:
questions.explanation: Ecologist Robert May estimated that the total number of species on Earth could be around 7 million, although only a fraction had been scientifically described.

questions.question: Match the trophic levels with their correct species examples in grassland ecosystem.
questions.explanation: Grass is the producer (first trophic level), rabbit is the primary consumer (second), crow is the secondary consumer (third), and vulture is the tertiary consumer (fourth).

questions.question: The first phase of translation is:
questions.explanation: Translation begins with initiation, during which the mRNA binds to the ribosome and the translation machinery is assembled.

questions.unit: Unit I: Diversity in the Living World
questions.question: Strobili or cones are found in:
questions.explanation: Equisetum produces strobili (cones) containing sporangia. It is a pteridophyte.

questions.unit: Unit I: Diversity in the Living World
questions.question: Match the following columns and select the correct option.
questions.explanation: Cyclostomes have 6–15 pairs of gill slits; Chondrichthyes have heterocercal caudal fins; Osteichthyes possess an air bladder; Trygon has a poison sting.

questions.unit: Unit III: Cell – Structure and Functions
questions.question: Some dividing cells exit the cell cycle and enter vegetative inactive stage. This is called quiescent stage (G₀). This process occurs at the end of:
questions.explanation: Cells may exit the active cell cycle from the G₁ phase and enter the quiescent G₀ stage.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement with reference to human digestive system.
choices: Serosa is the innermost layer of the alimentary canal.
Ileum is a highly coiled part.
questions.answerText: Ileum is a highly coiled part.
questions.explanation: The ileum is the highly coiled terminal part of the small intestine. Serosa is the outermost layer, and the vermiform appendix arises from the caecum.

questions.question: In which of the following techniques, the embryos are transferred to assist those females who cannot conceive?
questions.explanation: ZIFT transfers a zygote or early embryo into the fallopian tube, while IUT transfers an embryo into the uterus.

questions.question:
The plant parts which consist of two generations – one within the other:
(a) Pollen grains inside the anther(b) Germinated pollen grain with two male gametes(c) Seed inside the fruit(d) Embryo sac inside the ovule
questions.explanation: Anther with pollen grains, germinated pollen grain with male gametes, and seed inside fruit represent two generations in the stated arrangements. The embryo sac is the female gametophyte, while the ovule is part of the sporophyte.

questions.question: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs during:
questions.explanation: The synaptonemal complex dissolves during diplotene, when homologous chromosomes begin to separate and chiasmata become visible.

questions.question: Match the following:
questions.explanation: The Organ of Corti is located on the basilar membrane; the cochlea is the hearing organ; the Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the pharynx; stapes is a middle-ear bone.

questions.question: The ovary is half inferior in:
questions.explanation: Plum has a perigynous flower with a half-inferior ovary. Mustard and brinjal have superior ovaries, while sunflower has an inferior ovary.

questions.unit: Unit III: Cell – Structure and Functions
questions.question: Identify the basic amino acid from the following.
questions.explanation: The listed amino acids are glutamic acid (acidic), leucine (neutral), valine (neutral) and tyrosine (neutral). A basic amino acid would be lysine, arginine or histidine. The question appears to contain an error.

questions.unit: Unit VIII: Biology in Human Welfare
questions.question: Match the following columns and select the correct option.
questions.explanation: Eosinophils release granules containing histamine; basophils release histamine; neutrophils perform phagocytosis; lymphocytes are involved in immune responses.

questions.question: Match the following:
questions.explanation: Malonate is an inhibitor of succinate dehydrogenase; ricin is a protein containing peptide bonds; chitin is the fungal cell wall material; collagen is a structural protein.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement with regard to growth.
choices: Reproduction of an organism is an accomplished phenomenon.
Cell is metabolically active, grows but does not reproduce its DNA.
DNA synthesis or replication takes place.
questions.answerText: Reproduction of an organism is an accomplished phenomenon.
questions.explanation: Growth is a continuous, irreversible process, not an accomplished or completed phenomenon. Growth involves cell division, enlargement and DNA replication.

questions.question: Name the plant growth regulator which upon spraying on sugarcane crop, increase the length of stem, thus increasing the yield of sugarcane.
questions.explanation: Gibberellins promote stem elongation and are used in sugarcane to increase internode length and yield.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement with reference to the gene of human ABO blood group.
choices: A person will have only two of the three alleles of ABO blood group.
Allele Iᴬ and Iᴮ are present together, they express their own type.
Allele Iᴬ and Iᴮ are not present in any person.
The gene of ABO blood group has only one allele.
questions.answerText: Allele Iᴬ and Iᴮ are present together, they express their own type.
questions.explanation: The ABO blood group system demonstrates codominance: when Iᴬ and Iᴮ occur together, both are expressed, producing blood group AB.

questions.unit: Unit VIII: Biology in Human Welfare
questions.question: Identify the wrong statement with reference to immunity.
choices: When ready-made antibodies are directly given, it is called passive immunity.
Active immunity is given by injection of antigen.
When a person receives some antibodies from mother, it is an example of passive immunity.
When exposed to antigen (living or dead) antibodies are produced in the host’s body. It is called “Active immunity”.
questions.answerText: Active immunity is given by injection of antigen.
questions.explanation: Active immunity develops when the body produces its own antibodies after exposure to an antigen. Ready-made antibodies provide passive immunity.

questions.question: The enzyme enterokinase helps in conversion of:
questions.explanation: Enterokinase, secreted by the intestinal mucosa, activates trypsinogen into trypsin.

questions.question: The specific palindromic sequence which is recognized by EcoRI is:
questions.explanation: EcoRI recognizes the palindromic sequence 5′-GAATTC-3′ and cuts DNA between G and A.

questions.question: Match the following columns.
questions.explanation: Bt cotton produces insecticidal Cry protein; ADA is associated with gene therapy; RNAi provides cellular defence; PCR is used to detect infection.

questions.unit: Unit I: Diversity in the Living World
questions.question: Floridean starch is structurally similar to:
questions.explanation: Floridean starch, the reserve food of red algae, resembles amylopectin and glycogen.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not correct?
choices: The promoter has an extra peptide.
The function of insulin has A and B chains linked together by hydrogen bonds.
Genetically engineered insulin is produced in E. coli.
In a human insulin, A and B chains are synthesized as a single polypeptide.
questions.answerText: The promoter has an extra peptide.
questions.explanation: The promoter is a regulatory DNA sequence, not a peptide. Insulin consists of A and B chains linked by disulfide bonds; recombinant insulin can be produced in E. coli.

questions.question: Flippers of Penguin and Dolphin are examples of:
questions.explanation: Penguin flippers and dolphin flippers perform similar functions but evolved independently in unrelated groups, making them examples of convergent evolution.

questions.question: Which of the following refer to correct example(s) of organisms which have evolved due to changes in environment brought about by anthropogenic activities?
questions.explanation: Herbicide-resistant weeds evolve through selection pressure caused by human use of herbicides.

questions.question: Identify the wrong statement with reference to transport of oxygen.
choices: Partial pressure of CO₂ can interfere with O₂ binding with haemoglobin.
Higher H⁺ ion concentration favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin.
Low pCO₂ favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin.
Binding of oxygen with haemoglobin is mainly related to partial pressure of O₂.
questions.answerText: Higher H⁺ ion concentration favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin.
questions.explanation: Higher H⁺ concentration reduces haemoglobin’s affinity for oxygen and favours oxygen unloading. This is part of the Bohr effect.

questions.question: The process of growth is maximum during:
questions.explanation: Growth is maximum during the logarithmic (exponential) phase, when cells divide rapidly.

questions.question: Which of the following regions of the globe exhibit highest species diversity?
questions.explanation: Tropical rainforests, particularly the Amazon forests, exhibit extremely high species diversity.

questions.question: The sequence that controls the copy number of the linked DNA in the vector, is termed:
questions.explanation: The origin of replication (Ori) is the sequence where replication begins and controls the copy number of linked DNA in a vector.

questions.question: Match the following columns.
questions.explanation: The placenta secretes hCG; the zona pellucida surrounds the ovum; bulbourethral glands secrete mucus for lubrication; Leydig cells produce androgens.
